finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test passes the request-body field callback directly to axios.post, letting any client make the server send a request to an arbitrary URL, including internal hosts and cloud metadata addresses. The response status is returned to the caller.

trace.note: req.body.callback is used unchecked as the axios.post URL
r.status is returned to the caller, giving a status-code and timing oracle

finding.guards_checked: None in routes.js. No auth middleware on the pub router, no scheme or host allowlist, no private/link-local IP block, no port restriction, and no redirect control (axios follows redirects by default). Whether app.js applies global auth to pub is unverified because app.js is not in the directory.

verdict.guard_found: None in routes.js. requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) is applied only to the admin router via admin.use (routes.js:12), not to pub. No scheme, host, private-IP, or redirect validation exists before axios.post at routes.js:20.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: routes.js:19 registers pub.post("/hooks/test"), routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback unchecked to axios.post, and routes.js:21 returns r.status. No closing guard exists in routes.js:19-22, but app.js is not in the directory, so I cannot confirm whether global auth or other middleware is mounted in front of the pub router, and that decides whether the source is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker.

finding.claim: Admin-only GET /diagnostics/fetch passes req.query.url directly to axios.get. The admin session check is the only guard. An admin, or an attacker who obtains an admin session, can reach internal services through the server, and the status code is returned.
finding.source: req.query.url (routes.js:15, attacker-controlled query string, reachable only with an admin session)

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applies the role check to every admin route
admin.get("/diagnostics/fetch") registers the route behind that check
req.query.url is used unchecked as the axios.get URL
r.status is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-9, 12) checks session role only. This is an authorization control, not URL validation. No scheme, host, or private-address check, and redirects are followed. Severity is medium because exploitation needs an admin session.

verdict.guard_found: none for URL validation. The only check is the role gate at routes.js:8 (requireAdmin, applied via routes.js:12), which limits who can reach the route rather than validating the URL.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (routes.js:8, 12, 14, 15, 16), but the source fails the controllability test: req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only after the role check at routes.js:8 returns 403 unless req.session.role === "admin", so it is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker. The candidate's own "medium" severity note about needing an admin session confirms this.
